target_customer: Enterprise AI and data teams building RAG and agent applications over unstructured documents
problem: Generative AI applications perform poorly when fed messy, unclassified enterprise documents. Teams lack a way to create consistent metadata and quality scores for unstructured data.
business_model: Enterprise B2B software platform sold to AI and data governance teams
product_category: Data governance and metadata orchestration for unstructured data and GenAI

founders.name: Reece Griffiths
education: University of Cambridge, master's in information engineering
founders.background_notes: Product manager for an AI data governance product at QuantumBlack.

founders.name: Mikko Peiponen
founders.background_notes: Lead data scientist on an AI data quality tool at QuantumBlack.

founders.name: Leonard Platzer
founders.background_notes: Machine learning engineer on QuantumBlack's AI data quality product.

technical_complexity.rationale: Using LLMs to classify and score unstructured documents reliably at enterprise scale was hard but built on the founders' prior data quality tool at QuantumBlack, so standard engineering with some hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Metadata generation with LLMs was easy to approximate and big governance vendors could add it. Some advantage from enterprise integrations and prior deployments.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Collibra, a leading data governance vendor, acquired the company in July 2025 to extend governance to unstructured data.

market_need_then: In 2023 enterprises rushed to build generative AI applications and found unstructured data quality a bottleneck. TechCrunch in October 2023 described the product as ranking and filtering data to make generative AI more reliable.

branding.domain_note: Brand spelled Deasie while the legal and YC name is Deasy Labs; the site later used deasylabs.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Enterprise and metric driven, claiming for example 46 percent more accurate answers

brand_strength.rationale: Press covered the funding but no source shows brand pull, and the Deasie and Deasy spelling split suggests confusion.

outcome_analysis: Deasy Labs rode the 2023 generative AI wave with founders who had built a data governance tool at McKinsey and QuantumBlack, raised a $2.9M seed in October 2023 from General Catalyst and RTP Global, and was acquired by Collibra in July 2025 as the buyer extended governance to unstructured data. Terms were not disclosed, so the quality of the exit is unknown.
notes: The site now says it is brought to you by Collibra. Seed lead is disputed between sources (Seedtable says General Catalyst and RTP Global, another says Y Combinator). Acquisition date is 2025-07-24 in most sources, one aggregator says 07-15. Headquarters conflicts across sources. No dated competitor sources near the batch were found, since CB Insights competitor lists are undated, so the list is empty.
